chapters.before: Raise a frontier from the ashes
Vey’s engineers replace every fallen regiment. Cut their foundries and supply lines before their moving front reaches the valley.
chapters.after: Vey’s foundries keep his army supplied. Destroy them and cut his supply lines before the army reaches the valley.

chapters.before: The iron crown is lowered. Rowan leaves no throne behind, only three open roads and a watchfire that belongs to every village.
chapters.after: The iron crown is lowered. Rowan opens all three roads, and the villages take turns keeping watch.

chapters.before: Build a peace that can hold
chapters.after: Reopen the roads and river crossings

chapters.before: The crown is gone, but its abandoned toll forts still divide the frontier. Rowan, Sera and Iona must reopen a long road, settle the river crossings, and give the scattered settlements a common home.
chapters.after: Toll forts still block the frontier after the crown’s fall. Rowan, Sera and Iona set out to reopen the long road and river crossings so the settlements can trade again.

chapters.before: No banner claims the two bridges. The river charter belongs to every settlement, the distant beacons answer, and the frontier keeps its own watch.
chapters.after: The settlements share the bridges under the river charter. The distant beacons answer, and each village takes its turn on watch.

chapters.before: Stonegate opens. Beyond the pass, the smoke of a hundred furnaces darkens the sky.
chapters.after: Beyond the open gates of Stonegate, smoke from a hundred furnaces darkens the sky.

chapters.before: The furnaces fall silent. Vey retreats to the Crownworks, taking the last of his host with him.
chapters.after: Vey retreats from the silent furnaces to the Crownworks with the last of his host.

before.speaker: Captain Rowan
before.text: A barracks is a promise: hold this ground, and someone will stand beside you.

after.speaker: Captain Rowan
after.text: We’ll need warriors at the crossing before the next raid, so get a barracks up there.

missions.before: Put warriors in front and ranged support behind. Production keeps paying off as long as the building survives.
missions.after: Put warriors in front and ranged support behind. Keep your troop buildings alive so they can send reinforcements.

before.speaker: Scout Sera
before.text: The loudest fight is not always the most important. Look north. Then look south.

after.speaker: Scout Sera
after.text: Watch the north and south roads for raiders coming around the village.

before.speaker: Quartermaster Iona
before.text: Gold in a vault feeds no one. Spend enough to keep the mines working, and save the roads they pay for.

after.speaker: Quartermaster Iona
after.text: Keep those mines working so we can pay an escort for the relief wagons.

before.speaker: Scout Sera
before.text: A shield cannot stop a shadow. Give our archers a clear line to the sky.

after.speaker: Scout Sera
after.text: Bring archers forward to clear the gryphons over both roads before we enter the pass.

missions.before: The aeries empty. Sera’s signal rises over the pass without a single shadow circling it.
missions.after: The aeries fall. Sera signals the army to enter the pass.

missions.before: Stonegate has turned back armies for a century. Its three towers were built to stop soldiers, not an engineer with time to aim.
missions.after: Three towers guard Stonegate’s middle road. Bram needs siege engines and enough cover to bring them into range.

before.speaker: Engineer Bram
before.text: There is no unbreakable wall. Only a wall we have not reached with the right machine.

after.speaker: Engineer Bram
after.text: My engines can reach those towers if you keep the infantry off us while we aim.

missions.before: Bram’s engines open a path through the gate. The garrison abandons the stones it thought would last forever.
missions.after: Bram’s engines break through the gate. The garrison retreats, leaving the road open.

before.speaker: Engineer Bram
before.text: Their machines are excellent. Their crews still need something in front of them.

after.speaker: Engineer Bram
after.text: Hit those foundries before their crews bring up infantry to cover the engines coming toward the pass.

before.speaker: Quartermaster Iona
before.text: Every army has a heartbeat. This one is the sound of coin.

after.speaker: Quartermaster Iona
after.text: Vey pays for his reinforcements with those three mines, so that’s where we hit him.

missions.before: The ledger closes. For the first time, the marshal’s quartermasters cannot promise another regiment.
missions.after: With the mines lost, Vey’s quartermasters can no longer afford the reinforcements he needs.

before.speaker: Captain Rowan
before.text: We did not come this far to trade one ruin for another. Break the works. Bring our people home.

after.speaker: Captain Rowan
after.text: Cover our troops as they move in to take out the siege works.

before.speaker: Quartermaster Iona
before.text: One last camp. Make it strong enough that the next commander will not need to rebuild it.

after.speaker: Quartermaster Iona
after.text: Get the mines working before Rowan attacks; the siege crews will need food and reinforcements.

missions.before: The gates of the Crownworks open. The marshal offers no surrender, only one last army between the valley and its future.
missions.after: Vey has gathered his last army at the Crownworks. Break through and destroy his citadel.

before.speaker: Captain Rowan
before.text: No crowns. No conquered ground. We finish this so the roads can belong to everyone.

after.speaker: Captain Rowan
after.text: Bring down Vey’s citadel behind those walls so we can open these roads for good.

missions.before: Destroy the enemy citadel within 5:00. The marshal builds, upgrades and uses rally strikes. Your citadel must survive.
missions.after: Destroy the enemy citadel within 5:00. The marshal builds, upgrades and uses arrow volleys. Your citadel must survive.

before.speaker: Captain Rowan
before.text: Ending a war opens a gate. Keeping it open is the work that comes after.

after.speaker: Captain Rowan
after.text: Now the war’s over, clear those toll towers so the relief wagons can finally get through.

missions.before: The toll towers fall and the relief column reaches the horizon. Sera turns toward the beacons while Iona follows the river.
missions.after: The toll towers fall and the relief column takes the long road. Sera turns toward the beacons while Iona follows the river.

missions.before: Make room for a living frontier

before.speaker: Quartermaster Iona
before.text: Sixteen sites. Two bridges. Leave room for the people who will live here when the soldiers leave.

after.speaker: Quartermaster Iona
after.text: Leave room for mines as well as troops, and keep both bridge watchposts standing.

missions.before: The watchposts stand and the granary is funded. The river settlements sign a charter that makes neither bank a border.
missions.after: The watchposts hold and the granary is funded. Both banks sign the river charter and agree to share the crossings.

before.speaker: Scout Sera
before.text: Do not mistake a distant light for an empty road. Reach both beacons, then give them time to answer.

after.speaker: Scout Sera
after.text: The old crown still pays the companies out there. Cut off their pay stations and hold until the beacons answer.

missions.before: Attack both outer supply lines with ranged support against flyers. A central defense buys the long journey time; expand income before committing all your gold to the road.
missions.after: Attack both outer supply lines with ranged support against flyers. Defend the middle while your troops make the long journey. Build income before spending all your gold on the attack.

before.speaker: Captain Rowan
before.text: We are not here to choose a new ruler. We are here so no one can close these roads again.

after.speaker: Captain Rowan
after.text: Iona and Sera are bringing the delegates here, so hold the camp and keep both bridges open.

missions.before: The last toll works fall. River and beacon delegates meet on common ground, with no throne and no conquered bank between them.
missions.after: The last toll works fall. The river and beacon delegates meet at the camp to agree on how to keep the roads open.

missions.before: The commander pays for every reinforcement and reacts to your army. Protect the northern mine with a ground screen, retain archers against southern flyers, then upgrade a balanced force instead of exhausting all sixteen sites.
missions.after: The commander pays for every reinforcement and reacts to your army. Keep ground troops ahead of the northern mine and archers against the southern flyers. Upgrade your army before using all sixteen sites.

missions.before: The first snow is days away. Two working mines can fund the valley’s relief, but Vey’s outriders are already on the road.
missions.after: With the first snow days away and Vey’s outriders on the road, two working mines must fund the valley’s relief.

before.speaker: Captain Rowan
before.text: They are watching for that light. If it goes out, the army comes back for us.

after.speaker: Captain Rowan
after.text: Keep that light burning, or the army will turn back through the pass to look for us.

missions.before: The forward foundries are cold. Bram turns their abandoned tools toward repairing the road.
missions.after: Bram puts the abandoned tools from the silent foundries to work repairing the road.

missions.before: The camp holds. Every regiment receives its rations, and the siege crews prepare for the final road.
missions.after: With the camp secure and every regiment fed, the siege crews prepare for the final road.

missions.before: Both lights are still burning. Vey has no reserve left, and the army knows exactly where to go.
missions.after: Both lights guide the army toward Vey, whose last reserves have been spent.

missions.before: The Crownworks fall. The war is over, and the frontier belongs to the people who kept its watchfires burning.
missions.after: The fall of the Crownworks ends the war, leaving the frontier in the hands of those who kept its watchfires burning.

rhythmEdits.after: Watch the north and south roads for raiders coming around the village.

rhythmEdits.after: Keep those mines working so we can pay an escort for the relief wagons.

rhythmEdits.before: Gryphons over both roads. Get archers up here before we move through the pass.
rhythmEdits.after: Bring archers forward to clear the gryphons over both roads before we enter the pass.

rhythmEdits.after: Hit those foundries before their crews bring up infantry to cover the engines coming toward the pass.

rhythmEdits.before: Take out the siege works. Keep our troops covered on the way in.

rhythmEdits.before: We’ll need food and reinforcements for the siege. Get the mines working before Rowan attacks.

rhythmEdits.before: Vey is behind those walls. Once his citadel falls, we can open the roads for good.

rhythmEdits.before: The war is over, but the relief wagons still can’t get through. Clear those toll towers.
rhythmEdits.after: Now the war’s over, clear those toll towers so the relief wagons can finally get through.

rhythmEdits.before: Keep both bridge watchposts standing. We need room for mines as well as troops.
rhythmEdits.after: Leave room for mines as well as troops, and keep both bridge watchposts standing.

rhythmEdits.before: Hold the camp. Iona and Sera are bringing the delegates here, and they need both bridges open.
rhythmEdits.after: Iona and Sera are bringing the delegates here, so hold the camp and keep both bridges open.

rhythmEdits.after: Bram puts the abandoned tools from the silent foundries to work repairing the road.

rhythmEdits.before: The mines fall. Vey’s quartermasters can no longer afford the reinforcements he needs.
rhythmEdits.after: With the mines lost, Vey’s quartermasters can no longer afford the reinforcements he needs.

rhythmEdits.before: The company is assembled. Rowan leads the march to Emberwatch.
rhythmEdits.after: Rowan leads the assembled company toward Emberwatch.

rhythmEdits.before: One raider camp blocks the road. Your builders have brought plans for a barracks and an archery range.
rhythmEdits.after: Your builders can raise barracks and archery ranges to clear the raider camp blocking this road.

rhythmEdits.before: Put a barracks on the road. Build archers behind it if the warriors need help.
rhythmEdits.after: Start a barracks on the road, with archers behind the warriors if they need help.

rhythmEdits.before: The first road is clear. Wardens and miners meet the company at the fork.
rhythmEdits.after: Wardens and miners meet the company at the fork beyond the cleared road.

rhythmEdits.before: Choose a building in the build bar, then choose a site. Warriors move and fight on their own. Archers work best behind them.
rhythmEdits.after: Use the build bar to place a barracks for warriors who move and fight on their own, with archery ranges behind them for support.

rhythmEdits.before: One road. 420 gold. Build barracks and archery ranges at their normal prices.
rhythmEdits.after: One road and 420 starting gold, with barracks and archery ranges at their normal prices.

rhythmEdits.before: A Rootwarden can take a beating, but it hits slowly. Put archers behind it and keep an eye on the other road.
rhythmEdits.after: A Rootwarden can take a beating, but hits slowly enough to need archers behind it. Keep watch on the other road while it advances.

rhythmEdits.before: The fork is open. Siege crews, wizards and gryphon riders join the march.
rhythmEdits.after: Siege crews, wizards and gryphon riders join the march through the open fork.

rhythmEdits.before: A Warden lodge in front of an archery range gives the archers a durable screen. Barracks still work. Mines fund more troops; towers can hold a road.
rhythmEdits.after: Give your archers a durable screen with a Warden lodge ahead of their range, or stay with barracks if you prefer warriors. Leave space for mines to fund more troops and towers to hold a road.

rhythmEdits.before: Two roads. 740 gold. Warden lodges, gold mines and watchtowers join your barracks and archery ranges.
rhythmEdits.after: Two roads and 740 starting gold, with Warden lodges, gold mines and watchtowers alongside barracks and archery ranges.

rhythmEdits.before: Archers for those northern gryphons. Siege can reach the middle tower. Pick your route, but don’t lose sight of the other roads.
rhythmEdits.after: Bring archers for the northern gryphons, or try siege against the middle tower. Pick your route without losing sight of the other roads.

rhythmEdits.before: The way to Emberwatch is open. The full company is yours to command.
rhythmEdits.after: Take command of the full company for the open road to Emberwatch.

rhythmEdits.before: Rootwardens cannot hit flyers or protect another road. Wizard and siege splash can catch troops behind a screen. Use archers against air and consider siege or gryphons for the middle.
rhythmEdits.after: Use archers against air, and consider siege or gryphons for the middle. Rootwardens cannot hit flyers or cover another road, and wizard or siege splash can catch troops behind their screen.

rhythmEdits.before: Three roads. 1,100 gold. All eight buildings are available at their normal prices.
rhythmEdits.after: All eight buildings are available at their normal prices across three roads, with 1,100 starting gold.

rhythmEdits.before: The roads are clear. Rowan is waiting at Emberwatch.
rhythmEdits.after: The cleared roads lead on to Rowan at Emberwatch.

rhythmEdits.before: A raider barracks blocks the road to Emberwatch. Your camp is empty. Build an army and clear the way.
rhythmEdits.after: Raise an army from your empty camp to clear the raider barracks blocking the road to Emberwatch.

rhythmEdits.before: Put a barracks on the road. The warriors will take it from there.
rhythmEdits.after: A barracks on the road will send warriors to take care of the raiders.

rhythmEdits.before: The raiders leave the road. Ahead, the path splits around the hills.
rhythmEdits.after: Beyond the retreating raiders, the road splits around the hills.

rhythmEdits.before: Start with a barracks. An archery range behind it adds ranged support. Troops march and fight on their own.
rhythmEdits.after: Start with a barracks and an archery range behind it for support; their troops march and fight on their own.

rhythmEdits.before: One road. 420 gold. No starting buildings; every choice has its normal cost.
rhythmEdits.after: An empty camp on one road, with 420 starting gold and normal building costs.

rhythmEdits.before: They have a camp on each road. Check both before you spend.
rhythmEdits.after: Check the raider camp on each road before you spend.

rhythmEdits.before: Both roads are open. The scouts lead you on to Emberwatch.
rhythmEdits.after: The scouts lead you along the cleared roads toward Emberwatch.

rhythmEdits.before: Build troops on both roads first. A mine adds 2.5 gold/sec; a watchtower can hold a road while you build up.
rhythmEdits.after: Get troops onto both roads before investing in a mine for an extra 2.5 gold/sec or a watchtower to hold ground while you build up.

rhythmEdits.before: Two roads. 610 gold. No starting buildings; mines and towers use normal gold costs.
rhythmEdits.after: An empty camp across two roads, with 610 starting gold and normal mine and tower costs.
